prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on what kind of ad you need, your budget, and how much control you want. Below are top choices by use case, with quick pros/cons so you can pick what fits you.

Top picks (quick guide)
- Synthesia — Best for realistic AI presenters / talking-head ads
  - Pros: High-quality AI avatars, many languages, quick lip-sync; good for explainer/ spokesperson-style ads.
  - Cons: Less freedom for cinematic edits; enterprise pricing for heavy use.

- HeyGen — Alternative for AI presenters with competitive pricing
  - Pros: Good avatar selection, easy script-to-video.
  - Cons: Similar limits to avatar-style formats.

- InVideo — Best all-around for social ads & fast templates
  - Pros: Lots of ad templates, simple timeline editor, affordable; good for Facebook/Instagram/TikTok creatives.
  - Cons: Not focused on AI avatars or advanced generative effects.

- Canva (Video) — Best for teams/brand consistency
  - Pros: Brand kit, templates, collaborative editing, easy social export sizes.
  - Cons: Simpler AI features vs specialist tools.

- Pictory — Best for repurposing blog posts / long-form -> short ads
  - Pros: Auto-summarize and convert text/audio to short videos with captions.
  - Cons: Less creative control for custom animations.

- Promo.com / Shakr — Best for e-commerce ad scale
  - Pros: Retail-focused templates, huge stock asset libraries, ad optimization features.
  - Cons: Can get pricey at scale.

- Runway — Best for advanced generative/video effects
  - Pros: Cutting-edge generative tools and background edits; great for unique visuals.
  - Cons: Steeper learning curve; overkill for simple ads.

- Descript — Best for voiceover, editing & transcript-driven ads
  - Pros: Overdub voice cloning, fast transcript-based edits, screen recordings.
  - Cons: Not template-driven for finished social ad formats.

How to choose (criteria)
- Format & platform: vertical for Reels/TikTok, horizontal for YouTube; does the tool export required specs?
- Creative type: talking-head (Synthesia/HeyGen), template-driven social (InVideo/Canva/Promo), repurposed content (Pictory).
- Brand control: brand kit, fonts, color palettes (Canva excels).
- Voice/localization: multi-language TTS or voice cloning (Synthesia, Descript).
- Budget & scale: templates/apps are cheaper; enterprise/avatars cost more.
- Speed vs polish: templates = fast; Runway/Descript = more time but custom look.

If you want one recommendation now
- If you want the easiest route to scalable, high-quality social ads: try InVideo or Canva first.
- If you need a realistic AI spokesperson: try Synthesia (or HeyGen to compare cost).
- If you’re repurposing blog posts or webinars into short ads: start with Pictory.

If you tell me: platform (TikTok, Facebook, YouTube), ad style (spokesperson, product demo, animated text + stock), and budget, I’ll recommend the single best tool and a short workflow to produce a high-performing ad.
